subject: Banking
title: Foreign Exchange Trading
description: Learn Foreign Exchange Trading in one minute.

hook.text: The forex market trades $7.5 trillion daily. Banks handle most of it and profit from every currency conversion.

buildup.text: Corporations need to convert currencies for international trade. Banks charge a spread on every conversion.

discovery.text: Five banks control 50% of global forex trading. Citibank, JPMorgan, Deutsche Bank, UBS.

twist.text: In 2013, banks were caught rigging forex rates. Traders coordinated in chat rooms called 'The Cartel' and 'The Mafia.'

climax.text: Forex is hugely profitable because every international transaction needs a currency conversion.

punchline.text: $7.5 trillion daily. Five banks control half of all currency trades.

quiz.question: How much is traded daily in the global forex market?

details.summary: Banks dominate the $7.5 trillion daily foreign exchange market, profiting from the spread between buying and selling currencies. The largest banks earn billions annually from FX trading, serving corporate clients, investors, and governments.
details.whyItMatters: Every international transaction involves currency exchange, and banks sit at the center of this flow. The spread they charge affects the cost of global trade, investment, and remittances for billions of people.
takeaways: The forex market trades over $7.5 trillion daily, the world's largest market
The top 10 banks control over 70 percent of FX trading volume
Banks profit from the bid-ask spread on every currency transaction

faq.question: How do banks profit from foreign exchange?
faq.answer: Banks buy currency at one price and sell it slightly higher, keeping the spread. On trillions in daily volume, even tiny spreads generate massive profits. They also earn from advisory services, hedging products, and proprietary positioning.

faq.question: Why do banks dominate the forex market?
faq.answer: Forex trading requires massive capital, sophisticated technology, global client networks, and regulatory licenses. Only the largest banks have all of these, creating natural barriers to entry that concentrate the market among a handful of institutions.
